newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps fall as crude drops, mogas down $3.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps fall as crude drops, mogas down $3.

text.p: European oil swaps weakened on Tuesday as the energy complex turned southwards on news Iraq expected to resume oil exports within the next ten days.
Brent CFDs lost a few cents, fuel had a bumpy ride ending close to where it opened, gasoline dropped $3 or so while naphtha shed $2.
Dealers said the swaps weakness was related to crude's retracement.

CFDs for June 30-July 4 were put around -35/36 cents against August Brent compared with -30 cents on Monday. July 7-11 was pegged at -36/37 cents, about four cents off while July 14-18 was -35 cents against -28 cents. July 21-25 was also talked at -30 cents.
Heavy fuel swaps twisted and turned with July trading early in the day $1 or so higher at $83.50 before easing back to $82.25-$83. A later day July swap traded at $82.50.
August was heard done at $84 and $83.50 and $83.
Low sulphur swaps also ended down to $93 or so from high-points in the day when $94 was done for July.
Gasoline came under pressure losing $3 or so with July put at $178.50 and August and September flat. Dealers said $181 was done in the morning, but not repeated once crude came off.

Talk of demand from Nigeria failed to boost a lengthy physical cargo market. Nigeria was reported to be ordering the immediate import of 33 cargoes of petroleum products to end an acute fuel shortage.
Naphtha swaps shed $2 a tonne to $172-174 for July with a contango of $1 apiece against August and September.

Jet swaps were quieter after strong buying last week with 3Q put at $19-19.50, 4Q either side of $25.50 and 1Q98 at $26-26.50. Dealers said there was a fair amount of spread buying with the airlines also showing their hand for 4Q and 1Q98.
